title: Who to follow
summary: Recommends up to 300 accounts followed by the accounts you follow.
requirements: Add directed follows for Long account IDs; duplicate events do not duplicate graph membership.
Rank candidates by the number of followed accounts that follow them. Exclude self and existing followees, and return up to 300.
Select the top 1,000 candidates before excluding accounts already followed.
Recurring refresh eventually revisits the full keyspace.
nonfunctional: Recommendations refresh eventually. No write-latency target or measured efficiency claim is made.
constraints: Input IDs are Long; there is no unfollow operation.
The source cursor scans at most 15 accounts per task per tick.
invariants: Popularity counts followed accounts that follow the candidate, before the 1,000-candidate cap.
acceptance: After refresh, recommendations follow the popularity ranking, pre-filter cap, exclusions, and maximum size.
environment: A Rama stream topology stores follows; a microbatch topology computes recommendations. Test mode uses an appendable depot instead of the scheduled tick depot.
interfaces: create-module returns :module and :wrap-client; wrapper implements Synchronizable.
decisions: *follows-depot hashes by :from; *who-to-follow-tick is global and random in test mode or ticks every 30 seconds in production.
$$follows and $$who-to-follow are keyed by account; $$next-id stores each task's sweep cursor.
The who-to-follow microbatch selects a sorted range of 15 accounts per task, counts shared follows, caps candidates at 1,000 before filtering existing follows, then stores 300 recommendations.
tradeoffs: Paging bounds each tick's scan input and carries a cursor between calls; later ticks finish incomplete sweeps.
seam: The protocol adapter appends source Follow records and test ticks, then reads $$who-to-follow directly.
etls: core (stream): inserts each followed ID into $$follows[from].
who-to-follow (microbatch): pages through follows, counts candidate popularity, excludes already-followed accounts, and writes recommendations.
queries: No named query topology. Recommendation reads are direct client PState selections.

write: follow! appends to *follows-depot; core adds the target to the source account's set.

refresh! appends a test tick (production ticks every 30 seconds). Each task scans at most 15 source accounts from its cursor, counts two-hop candidates, caps at 1,000 before filtering existing follows, and stores up to 300 results.
read: recommendations(account-id) selects $$who-to-follow[account-id] directly; it returns [] if no value is stored.
flow.partition: *follows-depot and $$follows are keyed by source account. The aggregation reroutes by followed ID to read that account's outgoing follows, then hashes by requesting account for aggregation and output. $$who-to-follow is keyed by requesting account. $$next-id is a partitioned cursor PState.

caveat: A documented rseq-to-last compatibility change allows the full-page cursor to work on Rama 1.9 VectorBackedSortedMap. Same-module update retention is tested, not process-crash recovery or throughput.

title: Timed notifications
summary: Schedules posts by absolute time and adds them to account feeds when they are due.
requirements: Schedule a post string for a string account at an absolute millisecond time.
When the timer runs, deliver each post whose time is less than or equal to the current time.
Keep account feeds separate; delivery is asynchronous.
nonfunctional: The production timer is set to 1,000 ms. Tests use test mode and a simulated clock; production latency is not measured.
constraints: Inputs are strings and nonnegative absolute simulated-time milliseconds.
Order for posts with equal times is unspecified.
tick! is a test helper, not an application operation.
invariants: A tick before the scheduled time does not deliver a post.
A due post is appended to the feed for its account ID.
acceptance: Tests cover pre-boundary, exact due boundary, subsequent times, and separate accounts.
environment: Rama stream topology; TopologyScheduler owns scheduled entries. Production uses a 1-second tick depot; test mode uses an appendable global test tick and TopologyUtils simulated time.
decisions: *scheduled-post-depot hashes by account ID; *tick ticks every second in production or uses a random global append depot in test mode.
Topology core schedules each record by time-millis and appends due posts to $$feeds[id].
$$feeds maps account IDs to subindexed post vectors; feed reads the PState directly.
tradeoffs: The scheduler helper orders deadlines and scans for expired entries. Tests check simulated-time behavior, not helper internals.
seam: The protocol adapter creates ScheduledPost records, appends schedule/tick depots, and reads feeds directly.
etls: core (stream): schedules records with TopologyScheduler; on ticks, processes expired records and appends posts to account feeds.
queries: No named query topology. Feed reads directly select $$feeds.

write: schedule-post! appends ScheduledPost(id,time-millis,post); stream core schedules it with TopologyScheduler.
A production tick every second, or a test-mode tick, calls handleExpirations; due posts are added to $$feeds[id].
read: feed(account-id) directly selects all values at $$feeds[account-id]; it returns [] when absent.
flow.partition: The schedule depot and $$feeds are keyed by account ID. TopologyScheduler defines the scheduler PStates for timing index/state. Delivery routes to the account ID when updating its feed.

caveat: Behavior was tested with test-mode simulated time only. No restart/replay, fault-injection, delivery latency, or exactly-once behavior was established.

title: Top users module
summary: Totals purchase cents per user and ranks the 500 highest-spending users.
requirements: Add nonnegative purchase cents for each Long user ID.
Maintain up to 500 distinct users, ranked by cumulative spend in descending order.
Count every appended purchase; purchases have no IDs or deduplication.
Process derived state asynchronously; tests wait at a processing barrier before reading.
nonfunctional: No latency or throughput measurement is specified or claimed.
constraints: Purchase amounts are nonnegative Long cents.
Order for users with equal spend is unspecified.
Return at most 500 users, even when more have purchases.
invariants: Each user's total equals the sum of all appended purchases.
Each user appears at most once in top spending list.
acceptance: Check cumulative updates, descending rank for distinct totals, repeated appends, and the 500-user cap.
environment: Rama microbatch topology topusers with per-user spend state and a global top-user state.
interfaces: create-module returns :module and :wrap-client; wrapper implements Synchronizable.
decisions: user-spend-subbatch updates $$user-total-spend with +sum and emits updated totals.
Top aggregation routes updated totals globally and uses +top-monotonic with id-fn first, sort-val-fn last, and a cap of 500.
tradeoffs: Per-user totals distribute by user ID; the global top list requires global aggregation. The source updates it incrementally rather than recomputing all users on read.
seam: The protocol adapter creates upstream Purchase records, counts pending appends for microbatch wait, and reads $$top-spending-users directly.
etls: topusers (microbatch): adds purchases to user totals, emits changed totals, and updates the bounded global top list.
queries: No query topology. top-users reads the global PState directly.

write: purchase! appends Purchase(user-id,purchase-cents); user-spend-subbatch hashes by user ID, sums each purchase into $$user-total-spend, and emits new totals. topusers routes updates globally and applies a top-500 distinct-ID aggregator.
read: top-users directly selects the global $$top-spending-users list of [user-id,total-cents] pairs.
flow.partition: The purchase depot and $$user-total-spend hash by user ID. $$top-spending-users is global and single-partition; batch processing repartitions there for the ranking aggregator.

caveat: The contract assumes nonnegative purchases and does not deduplicate events. Recovery properties are not measured.
